q: Where does the CO2 come from when styrene monomer is made?
title: Styrene monomer CO2 per tonne
short: Most styrene is made by dehydrogenating ethylbenzene with superheated steam, so the main source is fuel burned in the steam superheater and boilers. Off-gas burned as fuel adds to it. Count fuel CO2 in Scope 1 and purchased benzene and ethylene in Scope 3.
audience: Petrochemical plants and buyers of polystyrene, ABS and SBR

ul: Fuel for the steam superheater, the largest single use.
Flaring during start up and upsets.
Benzene and ethylene, or bought ethylbenzene.

p: Toluene and off-gas leave the unit alongside styrene. If you split emissions between them, write down the method and use it every year.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
